caseTitle.en: The first sentence beside the incubator

condition.zh: 新生兒 · 疑似唐氏症

title.zh: 新生兒加護病房的遺傳照會
title.en: A genetics consult in the neonatal ICU

tagline.zh: 先說恭喜，再說他的名字，最後才說染色體
tagline.en: Congratulations first, then his name, the chromosomes last

desc.zh: 看寶寶、讀心臟超音波、數染色體，然後坐下來，和爸爸媽媽一起。第一句話要怎麼說，你今天會學到。
desc.en: Examine the baby, read the echo, count the chromosomes, then sit down with both parents. Today you learn how to say the first sentence.

desc.zh: 保溫箱、餵食、監視器，還有一位剛剖腹產完、第一次擠奶的媽媽。他喝奶喝到發紫的那一刻，你的手最先到。
desc.en: The incubator, the feeds, the monitor, and a mother expressing milk for the first time after a caesarean. When he turns blue during a feed, your hands get there first.

about.zh: 跟家屬說話一定先拉椅子坐下，從不站著俯視。口袋裡有一本小冊子，記著每個家庭聽到的第一句話。
about.en: Always pulls up a chair before speaking to a family, never stands over them. Keeps a pocket notebook of the first sentence each family heard.

about.zh: 會用一根手指讓寶寶抓著，同時看監視器。照會單寫得很精準，從不寫猜測。
about.en: Lets a baby grip one finger while reading the monitor. Writes precise consults and never puts a guess on paper.

role.zh: 新生兒加護病房小組長

about.zh: 每一個寶寶在她手上都有小名。今天 3 床的小名是她和爸爸一起取的。
about.en: Every baby in her care has a nickname. Today's bed 3 nickname she chose with the father.

about.zh: 三十四歲，國小音樂老師。昨天剖腹產，今天第一次坐輪椅來看寶寶。她說他哭聲像中提琴。
about.en: Thirty-four, a primary-school music teacher. Caesarean yesterday; today her first wheelchair visit. She says his cry sounds like a viola.

about.zh: 工地主任，個子很高，抱寶寶的時候整個人縮起來。他給寶寶取小名叫「石頭」，說要像石頭一樣堅強。
about.en: A tall site manager who folds himself small to hold the baby. He nicknamed him “Stone”, to be strong as a rock.

role.zh: 出生第一天的足月男嬰

about.zh: 虛構教學個案。足月出生，身體軟軟的，喝奶很慢。抓住別人手指的力氣，比大家想的大。
about.en: Fictional teaching case. Born at term, floppy, a slow feeder. His grip on a finger is stronger than anyone expected.

about.zh: 很愛孫子，也很怕。害怕的時候，會先找一個人怪。
about.en: Loves her grandson and is very frightened. When frightened, she looks for someone to blame first.

about.zh: 快速檢測當天出結果，完整核型要等培養。報結果時一定說清楚是哪一種。
about.en: The rapid test reports same day; the full karyotype waits for culture. Always says clearly which one she is reporting.

plain.zh: 多了一條第 21 號染色體造成的狀況。會影響學習、肌肉張力和一些器官，每個孩子的樣子都不一樣，很多人長大後上學、工作、有自己的生活。
plain.en: A condition caused by an extra chromosome 21. It affects learning, muscle tone and some organs; every child is different, and many grow up to attend school, work and lead their own lives.

plain.zh: 某一號染色體有三條，而不是兩條。唐氏症多半是第 21 號三體。
plain.en: Three copies of a chromosome instead of two. Down syndrome is usually trisomy of chromosome 21.

plain.zh: 肌肉軟軟的、抱起來像布娃娃。會影響吸奶和吞嚥，復健可以幫忙。
plain.en: Floppy muscles, like holding a rag doll. It affects sucking and swallowing; therapy helps.

plain.zh: 心臟中間的牆有一個大洞，上下左右都通，瓣膜也長在一起。唐氏症寶寶最常見的心臟問題，多半需要手術。
plain.en: A large hole in the heart's central wall joining all four chambers, with shared valves. The commonest heart problem in babies with Down syndrome; most need surgery.

plain.zh: 用超音波看心臟的構造和血流，不痛、不用打針，在保溫箱旁就能做。
plain.en: An ultrasound of the heart's structure and blood flow: painless, needle-free, done beside the incubator.

plain.zh: 用螢光探針直接數細胞裡第 21 號染色體有幾條，一兩天就有結果，但看不到染色體的完整形狀。
plain.en: Fluorescent probes count copies of chromosome 21 directly in cells; results within a day or two, but it can't show the chromosomes' full shape.

plain.zh: 把細胞培養後，把全部染色體拍照、配對、排好。能看出多的那條是自己一條，還是黏在別的染色體上。
plain.en: Cultured cells' chromosomes photographed, paired and lined up. It shows whether the extra one is free-standing or stuck to another chromosome.

plain.zh: 兩條染色體的長臂黏在一起。少數唐氏症是這樣來的，而且可能是爸爸或媽媽帶的，會影響下一胎的機率。
plain.en: The long arms of two chromosomes fused together. A small share of Down syndrome arises this way, and a parent may carry it, which changes the chance for the next pregnancy.

plain.zh: 下一胎再發生同樣狀況的機率。唐氏症的再發風險，要看是哪一種機制造成的。
plain.en: The chance the same condition happens in the next pregnancy. For Down syndrome it depends on which mechanism caused it.

plain.zh: 說「有唐氏症的寶寶」，不說「唐寶寶」或「那個唐氏的」。先是一個孩子，然後才是他的狀況。
plain.en: Saying “a baby with Down syndrome” rather than labelling him by it. A child first, the condition second.

plain.zh: 手掌上只有一條橫過去的紋路。一般人也可能有，只靠它不能診斷任何事。
plain.en: One crease running across the palm. Plenty of people without any condition have one; it diagnoses nothing on its own.

plain.zh: 從鼻子放到胃的細管子。寶寶吸奶太累時，把媽媽的奶從這裡慢慢灌進去。
plain.en: A thin tube from the nose to the stomach. When sucking tires a baby, his mother's milk goes in slowly this way.

text.zh: 保溫、保濕、隔絕噪音。側邊的小窗打開時，爸爸的大手剛好伸得進去。
text.en: Warmth, humidity, quiet. When the side port opens, the father's big hand just fits through.

text.zh: 心跳、呼吸、血氧。心臟有缺損的寶寶，餵奶時特別要看血氧的波形。
text.en: Heart rate, breathing, saturation. In a baby with a heart defect, watch the saturation trace closely during feeds.

text.zh: 吸不完的奶，從鼻胃管慢慢給。標籤上寫著：媽媽的奶。
text.en: What he can't suck goes slowly down the nasogastric tube. The label reads: Mum's milk.

text.zh: 推到保溫箱旁邊就能做。探頭很小，凝膠先溫過。
text.en: Wheeled straight to the incubator. A tiny probe, with the gel warmed first.

name.en: The little hat with his name

text.zh: 小羽用毛線織的，帽沿繡著「石頭」。佳蓉說，等他會走路，要帶這頂帽子去她的音樂課。
text.en: Yu knitted it, with “Stone” stitched on the brim. Jia-rong says when he can walk, he'll wear it to her music class.

name.en: How to say the first sentence

text.zh: 家長會記得這一刻一輩子。原則：盡早說，兩位家長一起，在安靜不被打擾的房間，寶寶在場或叫他的名字；坐下來；先說恭喜；先問他們注意到什麼；用「有唐氏症的寶寶」這種以人為先的語言；一次一點資訊，停下來讓他們問；給均衡、現在的資訊——包括挑戰，也包括很多人長大後過得很好；不要說「很遺憾」；提供書面資料和家長團體的聯絡方式；約好下一次再談。
text.en: Parents remember this moment for life. The principles: soon, both parents together, a quiet room without interruptions, the baby present or called by name; sit down; congratulate them first; ask what they have noticed; use person-first language, “a baby with Down syndrome”; a little information at a time, pausing for questions; balanced, up-to-date information, the challenges and also that many people grow up to do well; never “I'm sorry”; offer written material and parent-group contacts; agree when you will talk again.

name.zh: 為什麼快速檢測之後還要核型
name.en: Why a karyotype after the rapid test

text.zh: 快速檢測告訴你第 21 號有三條，但看不到第三條在哪裡。絕大多數是自由的三體，和卵子或精子形成時分離錯誤有關，再發風險低，與媽媽年齡有關；少數是羅伯遜轉位，第三條黏在另一條染色體上，其中一部分是爸爸或媽媽帶的，那時要驗父母的核型，再發風險會明顯不同；極少數是嵌合型。所以核型不是多此一舉，它回答的是下一胎的問題。
text.en: The rapid test says there are three copies of 21, but not where the third one is. Most cases are free trisomy, from a separation error while the egg or sperm formed: low recurrence risk, linked to maternal age. A small share are Robertsonian translocations with the third copy stuck to another chromosome; some of these are carried by a parent, so the parents' karyotypes are checked and the recurrence risk is quite different. A very few are mosaic. So the karyotype isn't redundant: it answers the question about the next pregnancy.

text.zh: 唐氏症寶寶出生後要看的事：心臟超音波（近半數有先天性心臟病）、餵食與體重、甲狀腺功能（新生兒篩檢加追蹤）、聽力篩檢、眼睛紅反射（白內障）、血球（暫時性的骨髓異常）、腸胃（腸道阻塞、排便）。之後還有發展與早期療育。這張清單是照顧，不是嚇人：每一項早點發現，都比晚發現好處理。
text.en: What to check after birth in a baby with Down syndrome: an echocardiogram (nearly half have a heart defect), feeding and weight, thyroid function (newborn screening plus follow-up), hearing screening, the eyes' red reflex (cataract), blood counts (a transient marrow disorder), the gut (blockages, bowel movements). Then development and early intervention. This list is care, not a threat: everything found early is easier to manage.

note.zh: 照會單上只寫看到的，不寫猜的
note.en: The consult records what's seen, not guesses

guide.en: Hear the consult from Dr Li

sub.zh: 3 床足月男嬰，張力低、外觀特徵，請遺傳科評估
sub.en: Bed 3, term boy, low tone, facial features; genetics please

lines.zh: 3 床，足月男嬰，出生第一天。張力低下、喝奶慢，有幾個外觀特徵。產前篩檢家長沒有做。
lines.en: Bed 3, term boy, day one. Hypotonia, slow feeding, some facial features. The parents didn't have prenatal screening.

lines.zh: 你照會單上寫「疑似唐氏症」了嗎？
lines.en: Did you write “suspected Down syndrome” on the consult?

lines.zh: 沒有。我只寫看到的。父母還不知道，我不想他們從保溫箱上的紙條知道。
lines.en: No. I only wrote what I saw. The parents don't know yet, and I didn't want them finding out from a note on the incubator.

lines.zh: 很好。這件事，要從一個人的嘴裡、坐著說出來。
lines.en: Good. This must come from a person's mouth, sitting down.

guide.zh: 整理 3 床的餵食幫浦

lines.zh: 石頭吸奶吸到一半就累。我們先準備鼻胃管和餵食幫浦，備而不用。
lines.en: Stone tires halfway through a feed. Let's get a nasogastric tube and the pump ready, just in case.

q.zh: 找到 3 床的餵食幫浦

post.zh: 標籤寫好了：媽媽的奶。她今天第一次擠奶，我們要讓她知道每一滴都用上了。
post.en: Labelled: Mum's milk. She's expressing for the first time today; we'll show her every drop is used.

note.zh: 特徵要合起來看，一個特徵什麼都不是
note.en: Features count together; one alone means nothing

lines.zh: 石頭睡在保溫箱裡，手腳鬆鬆地攤開。你伸進一根手指，他握住了。
lines.en: Stone sleeps in the incubator, limbs loose and spread. You slip a finger in and he grips it.

lines.zh: 眼角往上斜、臉部輪廓比較平、頸後皮膚多、手掌一條橫紋、第一和第二腳趾間距大，張力低下。
lines.en: Upslanting eyes, a flatter facial profile, extra skin at the back of the neck, a single palmar crease, a wide gap between the first and second toes, hypotonia.

lines.zh: 單一手掌橫紋，你我身上都可能有。哪一個特徵單獨能診斷？
lines.en: A single palmar crease could be on your hand or mine. Which of these features diagnoses anything on its own?

lines.zh: 沒有一個。要合起來看，再用染色體確認。
lines.en: None. They count together, and chromosomes confirm.

guide.en: The father is waiting in the corridor

lines.zh: 醫生，你們一直在看他的手和腳。是不是有什麼？
lines.en: Doctor, you keep looking at his hands and feet. Is something wrong?

lines.zh: 我太太昨天剛開刀，很累。有什麼先跟我說，我再決定要不要告訴她。
lines.en: My wife had surgery yesterday; she's exhausted. Tell me first and I'll decide whether to tell her.

q.zh: 爸爸希望先只告訴他。你怎麼做？
q.en: The father wants to be told alone first. What do you do?

options.zh: 盡快安排兩位一起談，媽媽在場
options.en: Arrange to talk with both, soon, mother present

why.zh: 大多數家長希望一起聽到；媽媽常常已經感覺到。由一方轉述，另一方會覺得被排除，信任也會受傷。
why.en: Most parents want to hear together, and mothers often sense it already. Hearing it second-hand leaves one parent excluded and damages trust.

options.zh: 先只告訴爸爸，由他決定
options.en: Tell the father alone; he decides

why.zh: 把重擔丟給爸爸一個人，媽媽也被剝奪了知道自己孩子的權利。
why.en: It loads the burden on him alone and denies the mother the right to know about her own child.

options.zh: 等報告確定再告訴他們
options.en: Wait until the result is confirmed

why.zh: 家長已經察覺大家的眼神和檢查。沉默讓他們更害怕；可以誠實說「我們懷疑，正在確認」。
why.en: They've already noticed the looks and the tests. Silence frightens them more; you can honestly say “we suspect, and we're confirming”.

post.zh: 下午一點半，家屬會談室。我們一起去，椅子我先擺好。
post.en: Half past one, the family room. We'll go together; I'll set out the chairs.

name.en: A hole in the middle of the heart

note.zh: 沒有雜音，不代表沒有洞
note.en: No murmur doesn't mean no hole

lines.zh: 聽診沒有明顯雜音，可是我們還是做了心臟超音波。為什麼？
lines.en: No obvious murmur on listening, but we still did an echo. Why?

question.zh: 懷疑唐氏症的新生兒，沒有心雜音，為什麼還要做心臟超音波？石頭的超音波看到什麼？
question.en: A newborn with suspected Down syndrome and no murmur: why an echo anyway? What does Stone's show?

answer.zh: 近半數唐氏症寶寶有先天性心臟病，最常見的是房室中隔缺損。出生頭幾天肺動脈壓力還高，左右兩邊的壓力差小，洞再大也可能聽不到雜音；等幾週後壓力下降，才出現喘、喝奶流汗、體重不增的心衰竭。石頭的超音波：完整型房室中隔缺損。早點知道，才能規畫餵食、追蹤和手術時機。
answer.en: Nearly half of babies with Down syndrome have a heart defect, most often an atrioventricular septal defect. In the first days, lung pressures are still high and the pressure difference small, so even a big hole may make no murmur; weeks later, as pressure falls, heart failure appears: fast breathing, sweating at feeds, poor weight gain. Stone's echo: a complete atrioventricular septal defect. Knowing early lets the team plan feeding, follow-up and the timing of surgery.

post.zh: 心臟外科會來看。現在的重點是餵食，還有讓他不要太累。
post.en: Cardiac surgery will come by. For now the priority is feeding, and not tiring him out.

guide.en: Prepare what to say about tests

lines.zh: 家長一定會問：「這個檢查會告訴我們他以後會怎樣嗎？」你怎麼回答？
lines.en: The parents will ask: “Will this test tell us how he'll turn out?” How do you answer?

post.zh: 染色體檢查能回答「是不是」和「是哪一種」；它不能回答他以後會說多少話、能做什麼。那要靠時間、療育和他自己。
post.en: The chromosome test answers “is it?” and “which kind?”; it can't answer how much he'll talk or what he'll do. Time, therapy and Stone himself answer that.

post.zh: 先說清楚檢查能回答什麼，家長就不會等一張報告來決定要不要愛他。
post.en: Be clear about what a test can answer, and parents won't wait for a report to decide whether to love him.

lines.zh: 聽力篩檢、眼睛紅反射、新生兒篩檢的甲狀腺、血球、排便。哪一項今天可以做？
lines.en: Hearing screen, red reflex, the thyroid on newborn screening, blood counts, bowels. Which can we do today?

lines.zh: 紅反射和血球今天；聽力篩檢等他穩一點；甲狀腺跟新生兒篩檢一起，之後還要追。胎便已經解了。
lines.en: Red reflex and bloods today; hearing once he's steadier; thyroid with newborn screening, and followed up later. He's passed meconium already.

lines.zh: 我寫在白板上。這是照顧清單，不是嚇人清單。
lines.en: I'll put it on the board. It's a care list, not a scare list.

note.zh: 先說恭喜，再說他的名字

guide.en: Sit down with Jia-rong and Zhi-ming

lines.zh: 雷主治先擺好三張椅子，關上門，把電話轉成靜音。小羽推著保溫箱停在門邊。
lines.en: Dr Lei sets out three chairs, closes the door and silences his phone. Yu wheels the incubator to rest by the door.

lines.zh: 這是最重要的一段。順序排出來，然後你說第一句。
lines.en: This is the most important part. Put the steps in order, then you say the first sentence.

q.en: Sharing the news, step by step

steps.zh: 安靜房間，兩位家長，坐下
steps.en: Quiet room, both parents, sit down

steps.zh: 先說恭喜，叫寶寶的名字
steps.en: Congratulate them; use the baby's name

steps.zh: 一次一點，停下來讓他們問
steps.en: A little at a time; pause for questions

steps.zh: 說明檢查與接下來的照顧
steps.en: Explain the tests and the care ahead

steps.zh: 給資料並約好下一次談
steps.en: Give materials; agree the next talk

post.zh: 恭喜你們，石頭很會抓手指。我們注意到他身體比較軟，還有一些特徵，讓我們懷疑他可能有唐氏症。我們正在用染色體檢查確認。
post.en: Congratulations; Stone has a terrific grip. We've noticed he's floppy and has some features that make us suspect he may have Down syndrome. We're confirming with a chromosome test.

lines.zh: ……我早上就覺得了。他的眼睛，很像我在特教班教過的一個孩子。謝謝你們讓我們一起聽。
lines.en: …I sensed it this morning. His eyes look like a child I taught in a special-needs class. Thank you for letting us hear it together.

lines.zh: 那個孩子……後來怎麼樣？
lines.en: That child… how did he turn out?

lines.zh: 會打鼓。打得比我好。
lines.en: He plays drums. Better than I do.

lines.zh: 我已經知道了。我在走廊聽到護理站在講。為什麼你們先告訴他，不告訴我？
lines.en: I already know. I heard the nurses' station talking in the corridor. Why did you tell him and not me?

lines.zh: 這是我們的錯。我們應該從一開始就請兩位一起。現在讓我們重新開始，好好說一次。
lines.en: That's our mistake. We should have asked you both together from the start. Let us begin again and tell it properly.

lines.zh: ……對不起，老婆。是我說要先聽的。
lines.en: …I'm sorry, love. It was me who asked to hear first.

lines.zh: 他會不會叫我爸爸？
lines.en: Will he ever call me Dad?

lines.zh: 很可能會，只是時間可能比別的孩子晚一點。早期療育越早開始越好。每個有唐氏症的孩子都不一樣，他會用自己的速度。
lines.en: Very likely, though perhaps later than other children. Early intervention helps most when it starts early. Every child with Down syndrome is different; he'll go at his own pace.

lines.zh: 還有，我們說「有唐氏症的寶寶」。他先是石頭，然後才是唐氏症。
lines.en: And we say “a baby with Down syndrome”. He is Stone first, and Down syndrome second.

name.en: The first bottle of Mum's milk

note.zh: 喝奶發紫：先停、扶起、抽吸、叫人
note.en: Blue at a feed: stop, sit up, suction, call

lines.zh: 佳蓉抱著石頭，第一次餵奶瓶。喝到一半，他嘴唇發紫，監視器的血氧往下掉。
lines.en: Jia-rong holds Stone for his first bottle. Halfway through, his lips turn dusky and the saturation on the monitor falls.

options.zh: 停餵、扶起、抽吸口鼻、依醫囑給氧、叫醫師
options.en: Stop the feed, sit him up, suction, oxygen per order, call

why.zh: 張力低加上心臟缺損，吸吞呼吸協調不好，容易嗆到或累。先停、讓呼吸道通暢，再評估是否改用鼻胃管。
why.en: Low tone plus a heart defect makes suck-swallow-breathe coordination poor, so he chokes or tires easily. Stop, clear the airway, then decide on tube feeds.

options.en: Pat him and finish the bottle

why.zh: 發紫時繼續餵，可能嗆入肺裡。這一瓶可以從鼻胃管給完。
why.en: Feeding on through a blue spell risks milk going into the lungs. This bottle can be finished by tube.

options.zh: 平放回保溫箱，等它自己好
options.en: Lay him flat in the incubator and wait

why.zh: 平躺不利於清口鼻和呼吸，而且要有人在旁邊看著處理。
why.en: Flat makes clearing his mouth and breathing harder, and someone must stay and act.

post.zh: 回來了。剩下的我們從鼻胃管慢慢給。媽媽，你剛剛抱得很好，是他的心臟還需要幫忙。
post.en: He's back up. We'll give the rest slowly by tube. Mum, you held him perfectly; it's his heart that needs the help.

guide.en: Sit with Jia-rong while she pumps

lines.zh: 我是不是連餵奶都做不好？
lines.en: Can't I even get feeding right?

lines.zh: 你擠的每一滴，現在正從管子進到他胃裡。鼻胃管只是幫他省力氣，奶還是你的。
lines.en: Every drop you express is going into his stomach through that tube right now. The nasogastric tube just saves his energy; the milk is still yours.

lines.zh: ……那我唱歌給他聽可以嗎？
lines.en: …Then may I sing to him?

lines.zh: 她輕輕哼起一首搖籃曲。監視器上的心跳，慢慢穩下來。
lines.en: She hums a lullaby softly. On the monitor, his heart rate settles.

note.zh: 快速檢測說三條；核型說在哪裡
note.en: The rapid test says three; the karyotype says where

guide.zh: 接實驗室電話並看核型
guide.en: Take the lab's call; read the karyotype

sub.zh: 3 床快速檢測：第 21 號三條
sub.en: Bed 3 rapid test: three copies of 21

lines.zh: 3 床快速檢測：第 21 號染色體三條。這是快速檢測，完整核型還要等培養。我先傳一張教學用的核型影像給你們練習。
lines.en: Bed 3 rapid test: three copies of chromosome 21. That's the rapid test; the full karyotype awaits culture. I'll send a teaching karyotype image for you to practise on.

lines.zh: 配對看看。多的那一條，是自己一條，還是黏在別人身上？
lines.en: Pair them up. Is the extra one free-standing, or stuck to another chromosome?

post.zh: 第 21 號三條，各自獨立。這張教學片是自由的三體。石頭的完整核型出來，也要一樣仔細看第 14 號。
post.en: Three separate chromosome 21s: free trisomy on this teaching image. When Stone's full karyotype is back, chromosome 14 gets the same careful look.

lines.zh: 所以下一胎就是四分之一嗎？還是二分之一？
lines.en: So for the next baby, is it one in four? One in two?

lines.zh: 四格圖是好用的模型，但它有適用的範圍。這一題，模型的限制在哪裡？
lines.en: The four-square diagram is a useful model, but it has limits. Where are its limits here?

post.zh: 唐氏症多半不是照四格圖遺傳的。再發風險要看是哪一種機制。
post.en: Down syndrome mostly doesn't follow the four-square pattern. The recurrence risk depends on the mechanism.

post.zh: 自由的三體，再發風險低，和媽媽年齡有關；如果是羅伯遜轉位，就要驗兩位的核型。
post.en: Free trisomy has a low recurrence risk linked to maternal age; if it's a Robertsonian translocation, we check both your karyotypes.

post.zh: 等完整報告出來，你們再跟我們說一次。
post.en: When the full report's out, tell us again, please.
Of course. It's already in the diary.

note.zh: 他先是石頭，然後才是唐氏症

guide.zh: 交班並聽雷主治的結語
guide.en: Hand over; hear Dr Lei's debrief

lines.zh: 3 床石頭：快速檢測第 21 號三體，核型待培養；完整型房室中隔缺損；餵奶時一次發紫，部分改鼻胃管；家長已一起告知。
lines.en: Bed 3, Stone: rapid test trisomy 21, karyotype pending culture; complete atrioventricular septal defect; one blue spell at a feed, partly tube-fed now; both parents told together.

lines.zh: 今天三件事：照會單只寫看到的；第一句話先說恭喜，兩位家長一起；快速檢測說幾條，核型說在哪裡。
lines.en: Three things today: a consult records what's seen; the first sentence is congratulations, to both parents together; the rapid test says how many, the karyotype says where.

lines.zh: 他打開那本小冊子，寫下一行字：「石頭，很會抓手指。」
lines.en: He opens his little notebook and writes one line: “Stone, terrific grip.”

sub.zh: 是不是媳婦懷孕時做錯了什麼？
sub.en: Did my daughter-in-law do something wrong in pregnancy?

lines.zh: 醫生，是不是我媳婦懷孕的時候吃錯東西？還是太晚生？我們家從來沒有這種的。
lines.en: Doctor, did my daughter-in-law eat the wrong things in pregnancy? Or have him too late? Nothing like this has ever happened in our family.

lines.zh: 阿嬤，多一條染色體是細胞分裂時自然發生的，不是誰吃錯什麼、做錯什麼。不是她的錯，也不是任何人的錯。
lines.en: Grandma, an extra chromosome happens naturally when cells divide. It isn't about what anyone ate or did. It isn't her fault, or anyone's.

lines.zh: 石頭現在需要的，是全家人一起抱他。他握手指很有力氣，像您兒子取的名字一樣。
lines.en: What Stone needs now is the whole family holding him. He grips fingers very hard, just like the name your son gave him.

lines.zh: ……那明天，我可以去看他嗎？我想織一頂帽子給他。
lines.en: …Then tomorrow, may I come and see him? I'd like to knit him a hat.

lines.zh: 你笑了。保溫箱裡，石頭已經戴著小羽織的小毛帽，帽沿繡著他的名字。明天，他會有第二頂。
lines.en: You smile. In the incubator, Stone is already wearing the little hat Yu knitted, his name on the brim. Tomorrow he'll have a second.

sub.zh: 先說恭喜，再說他的名字，最後才說染色體
sub.en: Congratulations first, then his name, the chromosomes last
